titleEn: Law on General Statute for the Military Personnel of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces

articles.en:
The Royal Cambodian Armed Forces comprise three branches:
1. the Army;
2. the Air Force;
3. the Navy. Article 4. The hierarchy of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces has three grades:
1. soldiers;
2. non-commissioned officers;
3. officers. Article 5. In the rank structure, the following ranks exist:
1. Ranks of soldiers — Army and Air Force | Navy: Private | Seaman; Private First Class | Seaman First Class; Corporal | Leading Seaman; Sergeant | Petty Officer.
2. Ranks of non-commissioned officers — Army and Air Force | Navy: Sergeant Third Class | Petty Officer Third Class; Sergeant Second Class | Petty Officer Second Class; Sergeant First Class | Petty Officer First Class; Warrant Officer Second Class | Chief Petty Officer Second Class; Warrant Officer First Class | Chief Petty Officer First Class.
[Page 2427]
3. Ranks of officers:
3.1. Junior officer ranks: Army and Air Force | Navy: Officer Cadet | Midshipman; Second Lieutenant | Sub-Lieutenant; First Lieutenant | Lieutenant; Captain | Lieutenant Commander.
3.2. Field officer ranks: Army and Air Force | Navy: Major | Corvette Captain; Lieutenant Colonel | Commander; Colonel | Captain.
3.3. General officer ranks: Army and Air Force | Navy: Brigadier General | Commodore; Major General | Rear Admiral; Lieutenant General | Vice Admiral; General | Admiral; General of the highest grade. Article 6.
Soldiers are assigned to two corps: Corps 1: the grouping of soldiers of the Army, the Air Force and the Navy who constitute the forces used in combat operations.
Corps 2: the grouping of soldiers serving in the administrative service of the Armed Forces.
These two corps may be divided into types of troops or specialised units.
[Page 2428]
Changes in the type of troops or specialised unit of a soldier shall be determined by sub-decree or by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence.
Promotion shall be made one rank at a time, and no honorary appointment may be made.

Professional soldiers are strictly prohibited: from using official working hours for private professional practice; from using the influence and power of their office to extract any benefit, or to threaten or violate the rights of citizens; from engaging in any occupation likely to affect the honour and dignity of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces; from becoming a member of the board of directors or of the management of a company in a private capacity.
Article 26.
Professional soldiers shall be assessed once a year. The immediate commander shall be the person who assigns the mark and makes the assessment, and shall inform each professional soldier of the assessment every year.
Article 27.
Each professional soldier shall have a personal file: papers recording his administrative situation; papers and other documents relating to decisions and declarations consistent with the statute or with discipline; the assessment marks in this file. The file may not contain documents stating the opinions or beliefs of the person concerned in matters of philosophy or politics.
Each document shall bear a serial number and shall be registered.
Article 28.
A person may be appointed as a professional officer only if he: has Khmer nationality; holds a certificate of good conduct showing a clean record; has the qualifications required to perform the duties.
[Page 2433] Article 29. The selection of professional officers shall take place at the officer training school, which selects candidates to study as officer cadets by competitive examination among students and by competitive examination among soldiers.
The conditions of this selection shall be determined by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence.
Article 30.
Promotion of professional officers shall be calculated on the basis of the period of service to date. Those professional officers shall be entered in the seniority list, which shall be arranged according to rank and according to their unit, in accordance with the seniority of those officers.

Promotion by selection or by seniority may not be made unless the soldier has served the minimum period and held the position of responsibility set out below: minimum period of service in one rank for eligibility for promotion to the rank of: combat soldier | soldier serving in the administrative service: Colonel; Lieutenant Colonel; Major; Captain.
[Page 2434] First Lieutenant | 4 years | 5 years. Second Lieutenant | 2 years | 2 years. Officer Cadet | 1 year | 1 year. The period for promotion may be shorter than the period set out above in necessary circumstances determined by sub-decree.
For officers of general rank, promotion may not be made under the above provisions but may be made according to the needs of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces.
A soldier who sacrifices his life or dies in the course of a mission shall be promoted posthumously.
Article 32.
Promotion of professional officers by seniority shall be carried out in each unit in the order of the seniority list.
Promotion by selection may not be made where the person is not named in the promotion list, which shall be drawn up once a year.
A commission shall be appointed by the Minister of National Defence, with the duty to report to the Minister on the necessary assessment and on the marks awarded by the commanders at each level to the person concerned.
Where a name cannot be entered in the annual promotion list, the person concerned shall have the right to be registered first in order of number in the following year's promotion list, unless the commission decides otherwise by a reasoned report to the commander in charge of that soldier.
[Page 2435]

Appointment and promotion shall be decided: by Royal Decree for the ranks of General and Admiral; by sub-decree for the ranks of Colonel and Captain; by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence for officers from the rank of Lieutenant Colonel and Commander downwards.
Article 34. A person may be appointed as a professional non-commissioned officer only if: he has Khmer nationality; he has served under contract; he has served for at least 4 years in the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces and already holds the rank of non-commissioned officer; he has the qualifications required to perform the duties. The appointment of professional non-commissioned officers shall be decided by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence.
Article 35.
The seniority of professional non-commissioned officers shall be counted from the date of commencement of military service to date.
Article 36.
Promotion of professional non-commissioned officers shall be made by selection, by seniority and in appropriate proportion. These conditions shall be determined by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence.
Promotion by seniority of professional non-commissioned officers shall be calculated according to the seniority of the person concerned in each unit and also according to the type of troops or specialised branch.
Promotion may not be made where the minimum period of service shown in the table below has not been completed:
[Page 2436] Minimum period of service in one rank for eligibility for promotion to the rank of: combat soldier | soldier serving in the administrative service: Warrant Officer First Class | 3 years | 4 years; Warrant Officer | — | —; Sergeant | — | —. Promotion by selection may not be granted where the person is not named in the promotion list, which is drawn up once a year by unit and sometimes by type of troops or specialised branch.
Promotion may not be made where the minimum period in the lower rank determined by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence has not been completed, except for persons of exceptional merit.
A commission shall be appointed by the Minister of National Defence, or by an authority to which the Minister has delegated, with the duty to report to the Minister the necessary assessment and the marks awarded to candidates by their commanders at each level.
Furthermore, where necessary, the period for promotion may be shorter than the period set out above.
A professional non-commissioned officer who sacrifices his life or dies in the course of a mission shall be promoted posthumously.
[Page 2437] Where a name cannot be entered in the annual promotion list, the person concerned shall have the right to be registered first in order of number in the following year's promotion list, unless the commission decides otherwise by a reasoned report to the commander in charge of that soldier.
Appointment and promotion shall be decided by a proclamation of the Ministry of National Defence.
Article 37.
The benefits of professional non-commissioned officers shall be determined by sub-decree.

Military status is lost where a soldier has requested discharge from the ranks with the agreement of the competent authority, or where a soldier has been transferred to the civil service, or where a soldier has been deprived of his rank by a court judgment.
A soldier who has ceased to hold military status as provided in point 4 of Article 38 shall be transferred to the reserve framework and shall retain the rank he already holds.
A soldier who has been convicted by a court shall not be included in the reserve framework.
Chapter 6. Soldiers under contract

Contract soldiers are persons who enter service voluntarily under a contract, with the rank of soldier or of non-commissioned officer, in the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces for: a specified period; the duration of a war or for a given period. The number and the conditions of recruitment shall be determined by sub-decree.
[Page 2439]

Contract soldiers shall be recruited from among persons who: have Khmer nationality, except in time of war; are at least 18 years of age; have the qualifications required to perform the duties.
Article 43.
A serving contract soldier may apply to renew his contract before the date of expiry of the contract.
Article 44. The rank, the status of loss of health or of working capacity, vocational training and the benefits of contract soldiers shall be determined by sub-decree.
